amienscathedral.name: Amiens Cathedral
amienscathedral.slogan: A stone Bible with room for two Notre-Dames.
amienscathedral.line: At about 200,000 cubic metres it is France's largest cathedral by volume, enough to hold two Notre-Dames of Paris.

thiepval.name: Thiepval Memorial
thiepval.slogan: Sixteen brick piers, and a name carved for every missing soldier.
thiepval.line: Lutyens' memorial, built 1928-32, bears the names of more than 72,000 men of the Somme who have no known grave.

pierrefonds.name: Château de Pierrefonds
pierrefonds.slogan: A ruin that Napoleon III's architect dreamed back to life.
pierrefonds.line: Napoleon I bought the ruin in 1810, and in 1857 Napoleon III asked Viollet-le-Duc to rebuild it.

julesvernehouse.name: Jules Verne's House
julesvernehouse.slogan: Forty voyages written under one brick tower.
julesvernehouse.line: Jules Verne lived in this tower house from 1882 to 1900 and wrote about forty of his Voyages extraordinaires here.

saintleu.name: Saint-Leu Quarter
saintleu.slogan: Mill streams and pastel houses, a short walk from the cathedral.
saintleu.line: Branches of the Somme gave this old weavers' and tanners' quarter its canals, and the puppet hero Lafleur was born here around 1811.
